==Usage==
<code><nowiki>{{WookDiscord|discordname=|name=|date=|messagelink=|quote=|archivefile=|nobackup=}}</nowiki></code>

<span style="color:red">'''Per [[Forum:CT:Citing Discord messages from Official Discords|this CT]], please make sure you drop all Discord screenshots&mdash;even from the Wook Discord&mdash;onto [[Wookieepedia:Discord screenshots]]!'''</span>

===Required parameters===
*{{Para|discordname}} Discord username.
*{{Para|name}} Full name of the Discord user.
*{{Para|messagelink}} Discord URL link to the message.
*{{Para|archivefile}} The uploaded Wookieepedia filename of the screenshot taken of the Discord conversation.

===Optional parameters===
*{{Para|date}} Date the Discord post was published online. In the format <code>YYYY-MM-DD</code>.
*{{Para|quote}} Quote of the Discord conversation.

==Example(s)==
<code><nowiki>{{WookDiscord|discordname=Holshef|name=Jack Mitchell|date=2021-11-22|messagelink=https://discord.com/channels/397848917036761090/492458000720592906/912207621069615104|quote=In the case of the statues in the emperor's throne room on Death Star II, that's an example of what they call 'ecphrasis,' the description of works of art as a way of giving background that's embedded in the narrative, instead of just having the narrator step back and say, 'OK, there was this guy Darth Bane&hellip;' So in this case I would hesitate to say that the poem was adding to canon by asserting that there were statues in the throne room &mdash; for one thing, none are visible in the film! Personally I would class them as neither canonical nor anti-canonical.|archivefile=File:Mitchell-Discord.png}}</nowiki></code>

Results in:

{{WookDiscord|discordname=Holshef|name=Jack Mitchell|date=2021-11-22|messagelink=https://discord.com/channels/397848917036761090/492458000720592906/912207621069615104|quote=In the case of the statues in the emperor's throne room on Death Star II, that's an example of what they call 'ecphrasis,' the description of works of art as a way of giving background that's embedded in the narrative, instead of just having the narrator step back and say, 'OK, there was this guy Darth Bane&hellip;' So in this case I would hesitate to say that the poem was adding to canon by asserting that there were statues in the throne room &mdash; for one thing, none are visible in the film! Personally I would class them as neither canonical nor anti-canonical.|archivefile=File:Mitchell-Discord.png}}
